newsitem.title: DUBAI: Iran expects inflation to fall to 20 pct this year.
newsitem.headline: Iran expects inflation to fall to 20 pct this year.

text.p: Iran's central bank governor expects inflation in the country to fall to 20 percent in the current year which started in March, the official Iranian news agency IRNA reported on Wednesday.
Mohsen Nourbakhsh "predicted that given the present trend of the country's economy, the inflation rate would be under 20 percent in the current year," IRNA said.
Iran's inflation in the last Iranian year to March 1997 stood at 23.2 percent against 49.4 percent the year before, IRNA quoted Nourbakhsh as saying.
Nourbakhsh also said Iran's gross domestic product had risen to 5.2 percent in the Iranian year to March 1997 from 4.5 percent the previous year.

"The growth rate figures for the industrial and mining sector were 5.7 (for the year to March 1996) and 6.3 percent (for the year to March 1997), while in agriculture, due to droughts in recent years, figures were 3.7 and 3.5 percent respectively," Nourbakhsh said in remarks carried by Ettelaat daily.

The central bank governor, addressing a seminar on monetary and exchange policies on Tuesday, also said Iran's imports were valued at 16.5 billion rials in the year to March 1997, up from 12.6 billion rials in the year before.
